gaps.what: Vassal tint of Joseon under Ming (1401-1637) and Qing (1637-1895) is not in this ledger; the suzerain dossiers (ming-dynasty ea-07, qing-dynasty ea-08) must carry vassal_start/vassal_end with counterpart joseon. Dates read: tributary system 1401, switch to Qing 30 January 1637, independence guaranteed 17 April 1895 (Joseon and Qing invasion pages).
Four Forts and Six Posts (Sejong's northern forts) have no year on any page opened; the 1433 expansion rests on one sentence of the Joseon page.

Imjin War: the Japanese retreat from Seoul and Pyongyang (1593) and the extent of the 1597 second invasion are undated on the pages opened (confidence 1 for the 1593 ends); the Imjin_War page loads only to July 1592.

Small Cliopatria shape changes (1415, 1516, 1622, 1632, 1860: 2-11 cells, mostly Jilin cells at the Yalu and Tumen) have no page; Treaty of Ganghwa 1876, Ulleungdo and the Russian frontier from 1860 not covered.
End of the wartime Japanese occupation (1905) is a bridge at the Eulsa Treaty; month and signatories of the Gando Convention (1909) are not on the Jiandao page.

Front line positions 1951-1953 are not on the Korean War page; the contest band on the 1953 line is confidence 1. The Korean Armistice Agreement and Korean Demilitarized Zone pages were not opened (budget).
The North Korea page prints 'established in the North on 10 July 1948'; used as the founding date but the reviewer should check it.
Same front-line gap as the DPRK; Liancourt Rocks (Dokdo/Takeshima) are only named as a dispute on the South Korea page.

problems: The Imjin_War Wikipedia page loads only up to July 1592 through WebFetch at any offset; the 1593-1598 events rest on Battle_of_Noryang.

Cliopatria shapes joseon_1595 and joseon_1636 are marked wrong: they draw the Japanese path (1595-99) and the Qing invasion corridor (1636-39) as territorial loss, the pages record occupation only. The rendering agents should use the corrections (full 1600 and 1640 outlines) and the ledger occupation/contest events.

Occupation and contest events for the Imjin War and the Korean War are recorded on both sides (owner and occupier) with the other party as counterpart, following the owner-side convention seen in ethiopia.json and empire-of-trebizond.json; warring-states-japan carries the Japanese side with different regions for 1592-93.
Joseon (Q28405 shared with gojoseon) and the two Korean republics (Q423 shared) are different states; no merge in any case.
The Joseon dossier used a tenth page (Tamna) beyond the 9-page budget, to settle the Jeju overlap with the tamna dossier.
The DPRK founding date follows the North Korea page (10 July 1948) and may be wrong.
